title: Immutable control plane swap playbook for on-prem clusters
content:
Purpose:
This playbook documents an immutable control-plane replacement strategy for on-prem Kubernetes clusters (mixed bare-metal and vSphere). The objective is to replace control-plane nodes without in-place upgrades to kube-apiserver/kube-controller-manager/kube-scheduler binaries, minimizing drift and avoiding long-running upgrade steps. Use when: control-plane nodes are old, kernel/firmware changes required, or when we want a clean control-plane image rebuild (new OS image, kubelet, or CRI).

High-level approach:
- Provision a new set of control-plane nodes in parallel (separate machines or VMs) configured to join the existing cluster as control-plane members.
- Promote new control-plane replicas to be read/write and gracefully evict workloads that implicitly rely on local control-plane footprint.
- Demote and decommission old control-plane machines immutably (destroy and reprovision if necessary).

Assumptions and constraints:
- Cluster uses an HA etcd topology behind kube-apiserver (either stacked etcd on control-plane nodes or external etcd cluster).
- CSI drivers used support PV migration or snapshots (we prefer to not move control-plane-local storage).
- Networking: BGP/metalLB or vSphere load balancer fronting kube-apiserver. You must be able to create a new apiserver VIP or attach new control-plane VMs to the existing LB pool temporarily.
- Terraform-managed infra: control-plane instances defined as a machine-type resource group (e.g., module.control_plane). We will create a parallel module instance for the replacement pool.
- CI/CD: an image build pipeline exists to produce a verified node image (OS + kubelet + CRI config).

Preflight checklist (run at least 24h before):
- Verify etcd health: kubectl get --raw '/healthz/etcd' or etcdctl endpoint health. All members healthy.
- Backup etcd snapshot and upload to offsite storage. Store checksum.
- Ensure cluster backup tool (Velero or custom) has a recent backup and restore tested.
- Confirm LB can accept additional control-plane backend servers without breaking session affinity.
- Gather critical manifests for static pods (if using static-control-plane pods), admission controllers, and any custom TLS certs.
- Check PodDisruptionBudgets for control-plane adjacent components (CSI controller, ingress controllers).
- Notify stakeholders and schedule maintenance window.

Terraform module notes (guidance to infra owners):
- Create module var: control_plane_pool_name (e.g., cp-old, cp-new).
- Keep control-plane instance group resources idempotent; allow two simultaneous groups for transition.
- Expose variables for: kubelet_version, kubeadm_config_template, apiserver_lb_pool_tag, ssh_key, provider_image_id.
- Use lifecycle.create_before_destroy = true for LB backend attachments when possible, to prevent LB downtime.
- Add a managed tag/label on instances to indicate role: kubernetes.io/role=control-plane and swap-phase=old|new.
- Add a resource: null_resource.join_script (local-exec) that writes a kubeadm join config to the new instances via remote-exec post-provisioning. Keep script idempotent.
- Plan for automated certificate sync (CA certs) so new nodes can join without manual CA export. If CA rotation is needed, plan follow-on steps.

Provisioning new control-plane nodes (outline):
1) Build and validate node image (image pipeline): latest OS patches, kubelet and CRI versions matching desired target.
2) In Terraform, instantiate module.control_plane with pool_name=cp-new and count matching existing control-plane replicas (typically 3 or 5).
3) Apply infra changes and confirm VMs boot, reachable by SSH and kubelet health endpoint.
4) Trigger join: run kubeadm join --control-plane --config /etc/kubeadm/join-config.yaml on each new VM (kubeadm token + discovery method). If using external etcd, ensure join-config references existing etcd endpoints and certs.
5) Validate new control-plane pods are Running: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=kube-apiserver; check logs for errors.

Traffic and leadership switch steps:
- If apiserver fronted by LB: add new control-plane instances to LB pool (Terraform / load balancer API). Verify healthchecks succeed.
- Verify apiserver metrics from new nodes: /metrics and audit logs.
- Monitor leader election status for controller-manager and scheduler (ensure new control-plane nodes can host leaders if configured).
- Gradually remove old nodes from LB pool (drain from LB); confirm no loss of API availability.

Handling etcd topology (stacked vs external):
- External etcd: join new control-plane nodes pointing at existing etcd cluster - simpler because etcd membership doesn’t change.
- Stacked (etcd on control-plane): either: (A) expand the stacked cluster by adding new etcd members (requires etcdctl member add on existing cluster, updating certs and endpoints) then remove old members; or (B) bring up new control-plane nodes that run etcd backed by restored snapshot from existing cluster on each new node, then rotate. Approach A is preferred for consistency; ensure etcd member add/remove steps are rehearsed and automated.

Data-plane (PV) considerations:
- Do NOT assume local-path PVs will move. If workloads use local-path, plan a pod-level migration to nodes with shared storage or recreate using PersistentVolumeClaims backed by shared CSI storage.
- For stateful components that depend on control-plane locality (some operators), coordinate maintenance or use replication controllers.
- Snapshot critical PVCs before any control-plane member removal. Keep associated annotations to ease restore.

Cutover: demotion and decommissioning of old nodes:
1) Mark old control-plane nodes with a label or annotation: swap-phase=decom.
2) Remove old nodes from the LB pool.
3) For each old control-plane node: cordon and drain non-control-plane pods (kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).
4) If etcd stacked, remove etcd member properly: etcdctl member remove <memberID> (followed by config updates).
5) Once workloads and etcd membership confirmed removed, power off and destroy old VMs via Terraform (apply with cp-old count=0).
6) Update monitoring, inventory, and asset tags to reflect new nodes.

Rollback plan (if apiserver availability drops or etcd becomes unhealthy):
- If new apiserver pool has issues, re-add old nodes to the LB pool (Terraform revert or API call) to restore API surface quickly.
- Restore etcd from snapshot to a recovery cluster if corruption or bad member removal occurs. Keep latest snapshot id in the offsite bucket for immediate use.
- Keep the old control-plane instances (do not destroy) until a full post-cutover validation window elapses (recommended 72 hours).

Validation and smoke tests post-swap (automated where possible):
- kubectl get cs / kubectl get componentstatuses (legacy) and kube-controller-manager health checks.
- Run cluster e2e smoke suite: scheduling, deployments, service LB, ingress routes, CSI provisioning and attachment.
- Run a set of operator specific probes (e.g., cert-rotation, controller-manager leader election).
- Verify audit logs for continuity and that RBAC rules behave correctly.

Operational notes and gotchas:
- Watch DNS TTLs for control-plane endpoints; some clients cache apiserver endpoints.
- Watch CRI runtime versions. Kubelet and kubeadm mismatches can cause join failures. Keep a compatibility matrix in repo.
- If static pod manifests are persisted on disk (e.g., /etc/kubernetes/manifests), be explicit about how they will be replicated to new nodes; do not rely on copying from old control-plane nodes.
- Certificate expiry: adding new control-plane nodes requires access to CA cert/private key or use of kubeadm certificate management helpers. Plan this step explicitly.

Postmortem template (short):
- Start time / end time of swap.
- Pre-swap snapshot id and location.
- Issues encountered and mitigation steps.
- Latency/availability metrics around swap window.
- Follow-ups and automation tasks created.

Open TODOs (for automation roadmap):
- Terraform submodule that can atomically flip LB pool attachments (create_before_destroy + staged lifecycle).
- A safe etcd member add/remove runner that checks quorum before confirming success.
- Automated post-swap smoke test pipeline gate that blocks cp-old destruction until passing.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: Priya Shah (eng-private-deployments)
- Escalation: Evan Martinez (SRE), Mei Chen (Platform Eng)
- Slack channel: #private-deployments

Appendix: quick commands
- Backup etcd (stacked): ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key
- Verify apiserver from new node: curl -k https://127.0.0.1:6443/healthz
- Remove node from LB (example): curl -X POST https://lb.api.local/pools/controlplane/remove -d '{"instance":"cp-old-03"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

End of playbook. Keep this doc as a living draft and iterate after the first swap run.
